question: In the IMNCI child algorithm, a mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) of less than 11.5 cm in a child aged 6–59 months, OR the presence of bilateral pitting pedal oedema, each independently classify the child as Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and trigger a Pink referral.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Under IMNCI nutritional assessment, MUAC <11.5 cm in a 6–59 month child OR bilateral pedal oedema independently satisfy the SAM definition. The MUAC cut-off is 11.5 cm — not 12.5 cm (which is the threshold for moderate acute malnutrition). SAM mandates urgent referral (Pink).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. SAM criteria include: MUAC <11.5 cm (6–59 months), weight-for-height/length <−3 SD on WHO growth charts, or bilateral pedal oedema — any one criterion alone is sufficient for SAM classification. SAM = Pink classification with urgent referral under IMNCI.
